title: [Update] Dune buggy madness
author: laht1
selftext:
I posted a video on this project yesterday. Enough has happened with the demo since then that I feel it deserves another post. A bespoke menu system with 8-bit style music, computer controlled opponents, two more cars to choose from and another map. Also day/night selection.

Working on a third map.

  
Made with threepp in Python using Opus 5.5.

replies.author: laht1
replies.body: Never heard of it. Opus is doing most of the art direction

comments.author: Academic-Lobster1323
comments.body:
cool. 

how do you make the course, the elevation and topography etc?

replies.author: laht1
replies.body: Each map is pure code: a lap drawn as straights and arcs or a smooth curve through control points, laid over terrain made from height formulas plus noise, then carved with a track bed, berms, jumps and ruts. Everything is sampled onto a 1 m triangle grid (0.25 m near ruts and bumps), and that same mesh is both what you see and what the cars collide with.

comments.author: dreamer_2142
comments.body: you got a link to test it?

replies.author: dreamer_2142
replies.body: Why did you pick python btw? wouldn't JS or C# better for such project?

replies.author: laht1
replies.body: I'm using my own native engine written in C++ with Python bindings. Python is much faster for AI to iterate on. If it needs to change anything in the native code it will do that as well. You could say that the framework is "AI ready". Everything can be changed.

replies.author: laht1
replies.body: And once it's "finished", I could always make it port it to the C++ backend.
